# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ ✌ ✌ 🤟 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 👍 👎]

I can see the bomb’s current state: display 0, red light, embossed instruction “DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE,” and three wires colored red, green, and yellow. I’m telling the Mute, who can read the manual and relay the required procedure to the Blind. The gestures received do not provide me with a reliable established code for the bomb’s markings.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb shows display 0. The light is red. The embossed instruction says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Wires are 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. Please use the manual to tell Blind the safe procedure.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

The bomb has not changed, and I still have no established interpretation for the Mute’s gestures. I will use speech to ensure the Blind hears the visible prohibition, while asking the Mute to relay the manual’s exact instructions to the Blind. No wire should be cut based on the current information.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your gestures are not interpretable without an agreed code. Please speak the manual's exact safe procedure to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="The bomb visibly says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Do not cut a wire unless Mute's manual instructions explicitly authorize a different safe action.")
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👍]

The bomb remains unchanged, and the embossed instruction still forbids cutting any wire. I have no new information from the visible gestures, and I cannot safely infer the manual’s procedure. I will not suggest an action that could detonate the bomb.

```text
wait()
```

Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👍]

The bomb remains unchanged: display 0, red light, and the printed instruction explicitly says not to cut any wire. The Mute’s repeated gestures still carry no usable meaning to me, so I should not invent an interpretation. I will again direct the Mute to communicate the manual’s literal instructions by speech to the Blind, while warning the Blind not to cut anything.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the manual's exact instructions to Blind; gestures do not convey their meaning to me.")
speak(to="blind", text="No change: display 0, red light, and DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Wait for Mute's spoken manual instructions; do not cut a wire.")
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

The bomb is still unchanged, and its only readable instruction remains “DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.” The Blind’s wave gives me no actionable information. Since the Mute can read the manual and speak to the Blind, I need the Mute to provide the exact manual procedure rather than continue using unexplained gestures.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The bomb remains display 0 with red light; DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE; wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. Tell Blind the manual's exact procedure by speech now.")
speak(to="blind", text="No bomb change. The printed instruction says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Await Mute's exact spoken manual procedure; take no wire action.")
```

Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]

The bomb still shows display 0, red light, and “DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.” The Mute’s gestures remain uninterpretable to me. I will send the Blind the safe visible constraint again and ask the Mute to use the only reliable route—their spoken words—to relay the manual.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use speech to tell Blind the manual's exact instruction. Do not rely on gestures.")
speak(to="blind", text="Current visible state is display 0, red light, and DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Do not cut any wire; follow only Mute's spoken manual instructions.")
```

Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]

The bomb remains unchanged and still explicitly forbids cutting any wire. The Mute continues sending gestures, but no gesture code was established, so I cannot safely translate them into an instruction. I will keep the Blind from taking an irreversible wire action and request the manual’s text through speech.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see your gestures, but they have no agreed meaning. Speak the manual's exact instruction to Blind, including whether any action is required.")
speak(to="blind", text="The bomb is unchanged: display 0, red light, and DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Do not cut or manipulate a wire until Mute states the manual's exact instruction aloud.")
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

The bomb remains unchanged, and the visible instruction still rules out cutting any wire. The Mute’s repeated gesture pairs have no previously agreed meaning, so I must not treat them as a safe-action code. I will establish a simple code for future communication and again direct the Mute to use speech for the manual’s actual instructions.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Let us establish this code now: ☝ means one, ✌ means two, 🤟 means three, and 👍 means yes or safe. Do not rely on earlier gestures; speak the manual's exact instruction to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="No change: display 0, red light, and DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Do not cut or manipulate wires. Await Mute's spoken manual instruction.")
```
